knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 3.3.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. (1) What is a null hypothesis vs an alternative? (2) What is a type I error vs a type II error? (3) What does a p-value measure, and what is power? (4) Name one reason a basic applied test is not today's LO.
hints: Use CMP language from today's notes.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Null is the statement under test; alternative is the competing claim. Type I is rejecting a true null; type II is failing to reject a false null. A p-value is the probability, under the null, of a result at least as extreme as observed; power is the probability of rejecting a false null. Applied cookbook tests are tomorrow's LO.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Skipping the LO hinge or swallowing the next LO.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 3.3.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Disease screening: H₀ = no disease, H₁ = disease present. (1) Define Type I and Type II errors in this vignette. (2) What does a p-value measure, and what is power? (3) Refuse: 'I ran a one-sample Normal mean test in software, so the concepts LO is done.'
knowledge_checks.body: HT vocabulary on a vignette; refuse cookbook-test-as-concepts.
knowledge_checks.explanation: 3.3.1 is conceptual toolkit (errors, p-value, power) not yet the applied cookbook tests.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: (1) Type I: false positive (declare disease when healthy (reject H₀ wrongly). Type II: false negative) miss disease when present (fail to reject H₀ wrongly). (2) p-value: under H₀, the probability of a result at least as extreme as observed. Power: P(reject H₀ | H₁ true) = 1 − β. (3) Refuse: running a cookbook test is not the same as mastering HT vocabulary (errors, critical region, p-value, power).
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Skipping vocabulary for a cookbook z-test, or swapping Type I and Type II.
success_criteria: Defines Type I/II correctly on the vignette and states p-value and power.
Refuses treating an applied software test as finishing concepts.
